↳ Posted by gian marco on July 20th, 2002.

Names of Paddy Fahy Tunes

Paddy Fahy did not give names to any of his compositions. This particular jig appears neither on “d flute album” nor on “In Good Company” by Kevin Crawford as the Paddy Fahy tunes on these albums are respectively a hornpipe and a reel. I presume that the information on recordings is added by an automatic process and the result is a list of all recordings in the database entitled “Paddy Fahy’s” rather than a list of recordings of this particular tune which, by the way, doesn’t sound like a Paddy Fahy tune to my ear.

Paddy Fahy

Paddy would be in his seventies but as far as I know is still going strong. He’s a composer of many tunes most of which are very distinctive with their use of accidentals (F naturals and B flat, etc) although frustratingly they’re rarely given names - how many Paddy Fahy reels have you heard of? Hopefully he’ll continue composing these wonderful tunes.

↳ Posted by Ian Varley on March 14th, 2020.

Re: Paddy Fahey’s

https://thesession.org/tunes/124
This Paddy Fahey jig in D major is not included as one of 12 jigs in Maria Holohan’s 1995 U. of Limerick M. A. thesis on the compositions of Paddy Fahey. Therefore it lacks a number designation, according to the system that Holohan proposed for the tunes; - one system anyway that is available to avoid confusion among them. This is NOT a version of Fahey’s jig #1 according to this system. #13 is more apropos.
The tune seems to have been popular among musicians for a while, prompting a question or two:
Is this truly a Fahey tune that escaped Holohan’s notice and if so, why?
Is there documentation (bootleg tape, etc.) that he actually composed it?

Re: Paddy Fahey’s

The earliest recording I can find is ”Back Home to the Cliffs of Moher” from 1972, and there it’s the first tune in a set called Fahy’s Jigs 1 & 2.

After that, ”The Rushy Mountain” from 1977, as part of set called Matt Haye’s Jigs. My CDs are buried in cardboard boxes, so I can’t check the liner notes.

Maybe there’s some information to be found.
